args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 (deployed to production in us-east, us-west, eu-west) was failing health checks with an error rate of ~18%. Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release marked healthy in production. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging prior to the production deploy. Follow-up: verify recovery post-rollback and investigate root cause in v2.3.1.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release marked healthy in production, so I rolled back to it. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It explains the failure, the rollback and the regions affected. It also notes that v2.3.1's release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was already unhealthy in staging before it went to production.
- **Incident text is out of date:** I opened the incident while checking the service, so its summary still lists confirming recovery as a follow-up. That's now confirmed, so the remaining follow-up is finding what broke in v2.3.1.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
